note: Rewritten from the redescription by Syaukani et al. (2019) based on specimens from Indonesia; only the soldier and worker castes are described, the original account has no alate. Soldier measurements are the range for 12 specimens from 6 colonies.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body small. Head (excluding nasus) oval, slightly longer than wide, without a constriction behind the antennae; dorsal surface of the head flat or slightly concave, rising gently toward the tip of the nasus. Nasus long and cylindrical, more than half the length of the head capsule, nasus index 0.68–0.73; tip of the nasus with several hairs and 4 short setae. Antennae 12-segmented, segment 3 slightly longer than segment 2, segments 3 and 4 subequal, segments 5–12 gradually lengthening toward the tip. Mandibles without a projecting tooth at the tip. Pronotum saddle-shaped, without projections on the anterior or posterior margin. Legs short. Head pale yellow to yellowish brown, nasus reddish brown, antennae yellow, pronotum pale yellow, abdominal tergites and legs pale yellow; a pair of setae on the posterior part of the head. Measurements (mm): head including nasus 1.47–1.49, head without nasus 0.89–0.91, maximum head width 0.76–0.82, maximum head height 0.51–0.53, pronotum length 0.15–0.17, pronotum width 0.42–0.44.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body minute, integument semi-transparent. Left mandible: apical tooth very large and fused with the first tooth, the main diagnostic character of the species; second tooth well developed; third tooth not projecting or appearing level; fourth tooth not visible from the front, overlapping the molar tooth; molar tooth slightly elliptical. Right mandible: anterior margin of the first tooth rather straight or slightly concave at the base; second tooth undeveloped, a character specific to O. inanis; molar notch well developed, its upper and lower lamellae of unequal thickness, outer margin of the molar tooth distinctly concave. No worker measurements were given in the original account.
